- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Routes mHC through the `ResidualConnection` contract refined in #8657, so mHC and Wide Residuals share Transformer-layer scheduling. The dedicated mHC layer inherits the base attention and MLP schedules instead of duplicating them.

## Changes

- Add parameterless read/write adapters that invoke the existing mHC owners and carry the residual and predicted maps between operations. Parameter names, state-dict keys, and owner hooks are preserved.
- Share one numerical write helper between eager execution and checkpoint replay. Output-discard replay covers aggregation and nonterminal writes; projection retains its independent checkpoint.
- Preserve mHC's residual selection, norm checkpointing, gradient scopes, and terminal-write behavior through the shared schedule.

The existing mHC manager entry point remains in use; manager/context unification is deferred to the layer PR.

## Issue tracking

Unification design proposal: #7888.
Depends on #8657.

## Code provenance

Refactors existing Megatron-LM code. No code copied from external repositories.

This was a light review. I found nothing the light rubric asks me to flag in the four changed files. I read the source but did not run any tests. I checked the following:

- **Write arithmetic is unchanged.** [`_compute_write`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/6aeb88cda3fe008b749c7fd34da322c1307e0200/megatron/core/transformer/hyper_connection.py#L819-L869) performs the same steps as the old eager write [`_fused_h_res_h_post_bda_native`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/ac5dd916646b8000eddb77fe5ddfb57e7905cc33/megatron/core/transformer/hyper_connection.py#L749-L798), for both the dropout-free kernel and the dropout fallback. That includes the final `.to(original_residual.dtype)`.
- **Passing `bias=None` to the checkpoint is safe.** `_ArgLayout` keeps arguments that are not tensors outside autograd, and replay rebuilds them in place.
- **FP8 setting matches the old code.** Both `ResidualStreamRecomputeContext.checkpoint` and `_resolve_mhc_checkpoint` create `CheckpointWithoutOutput` with `fp8=False`, which is what the old code used.
- **The params-dtype cast in `_write_to_owner` cannot be reached** under a validated config. `TransformerConfig` already rejects mHC combined with `fp32_residual_connection`.
- **The shared layer path behaves like the removed overrides** in [`hyper_connection_transformer_layer.py`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/6aeb88cda3fe008b749c7fd34da322c1307e0200/megatron/core/transformer/hyper_connection_transformer_layer.py#L207-L264). The norm checkpoints use the same manager. Norm offload and its `group_offload` commit still happen. Writes still run inside `bias_dropout_add_exec_handler`. The last MLP write in a recompute block still runs eagerly. A norm that returns a residual is still rejected.
- **Dropping the old pre-MLP-norm discard changes nothing.** That checkpoint always had a manager in that case, and `discard_output_and_register_recompute` does nothing when a manager is set.
- **Other callers still work with the new signatures.** `HyperConnectionHybridLayer` and the existing mHC tests still call `HyperConnectionModule.forward`, `_forward_with_checkpoint` and `fused_h_res_h_post_bda` in ways the new signatures accept.
- **Tests and conventions.** The two new test files cover the adapters' read/write state, checkpoint registration counts and replay equivalence. The GPU-only tests are skipped when CUDA is unavailable. The change has no new global process-group access and adds or changes no GPU kernel, so no determinism test is needed.

One limitation: the report from the reviewer covering `hyper_connection.py` did not come back, so I reviewed that file myself.

# What does this PR do?

Routes mHC through the `ResidualConnection` contract refined in #8657, so mHC and Wide Residuals share Transformer-layer scheduling. The dedicated mHC layer inherits the base attention and MLP schedules instead of duplicating them.

## Changes

- Add parameterless read/write adapters that invoke the existing mHC owners and carry the residual and predicted maps between operations. Parameter names, state-dict keys, and owner hooks are preserved.
- Share one numerical write helper between eager execution and checkpoint replay. Output-discard replay covers aggregation and nonterminal writes; projection retains its independent checkpoint.
- Preserve mHC's residual selection, norm checkpointing, gradient scopes, and terminal-write behavior through the shared schedule.

The existing mHC manager entry point remains in use; manager/context unification is deferred to the layer PR.

## Issue tracking

Unification design proposal: #7888.
Depends on #8657.

## Code provenance

Refactors existing Megatron-LM code. No code copied from external repositories.

That includes the final `.to(original_residual.dtype)`.
- **Passing `bias=None` to the checkpoint is safe.** `_ArgLayout` keeps arguments that are not tensors outside autograd, and replay rebuilds them in place.
- **FP8 setting matches the old code.** Both `ResidualStreamRecomputeContext.checkpoint` and `_resolve_mhc_checkpoint` create `CheckpointWithoutOutput` with `fp8=False`, which is what the old code used.
- **The params-dtype cast in `_write_to_owner` cannot be reached** under a validated config. `TransformerConfig` already rejects mHC combined with `fp32_residual_connection`.
- **The shared layer path behaves like the removed overrides** in [`hyper_connection_transformer_layer.py`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/6aeb88cda3fe008b749c7fd34da322c1307e0200/megatron/core/transformer/hyper_connection_transformer_layer.py#L207-L264). The last MLP write in a recompute block still runs eagerly. A norm that returns a residual is still rejected.
- **Dropping the old pre-MLP-norm discard changes nothing.** That checkpoint always had a manager in that case, and `discard_output_and_register_recompute` does nothing when a manager is set.
- **Other callers still work with the new signatures.** `HyperConnectionHybridLayer` and the existing mHC tests still call `HyperConnectionModule.forward`, `_forward_with_checkpoint` and `fused_h_res_h_post_bda` in ways the new signatures accept.
- **Tests and conventions.** The two new test files cover the adapters' read/write state, checkpoint registration counts and replay equivalence. The GPU-only tests are skipped when CUDA is unavailable. The change has no new global process-group access and adds or changes no GPU kernel, so no determinism test is needed.
